title: Gravitational field strength
target: Use a gravitational field to predict the force on a test mass.
criteria: Distinguish source field from the mass placed in it.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: At a point north of a spherical planet, which way does its gravitational field point?
options: No direction because a field is a scalar.
cpa.guide: The gravitational field gives the force direction on a positive test mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Two nearby field arrows point toward a source, but one is longer under a stated strength scale. What does the longer arrow mean?
cpa.guide: With that scale, arrow length represents field magnitude.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A 3 kg test mass experiences 21 N of gravitational force. What is g?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: At a location with g = 6 N/kg, what force acts on a 5 kg test mass?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A test mass is replaced by one three times as large, without changing the source or location. What changes?
options: Field strength triples; force stays the same.
Force triples; source field strength stays the same.
cpa.guide: g = GM/r² depends on the source and location; F = mg depends on test mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Two test masses at the same location give F/m = 4 N/kg in separate trials. What does that support?
options: A common source field independent of the chosen test mass.
Zero gravitational force on both masses.
Force and mass are the same physical quantity.
A field that doubles with every test mass.
cpa.guide: The ratio F/m identifies field strength.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
